memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Of the animals that move along the ground, these are unclean for you: the weasel, the rat, any kind of great lizard, the gecko, the monitor lizard, the wall lizard, the skink and the chameleon. Of all those that move along the ground, these are unclean for you. Whoever touches them when they are dead will be unclean till evening." - Lev 11:29-31 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Weasels, rats, geckos, lizards on the wall. These were not exotic creatures Israel had to travel to see. They were house guests — the things that scuttled through a home in the evening, that a child might find behind a jar.

God is dealing here with what is close. Not distant dangers, but the ones that live in the walls of your own house.

Spiritually, that is often where our real battles are. It is easy to be alarmed about great evils far away, and blind to the small things running loose at home — the sharp word to a spouse, the impatience with an ageing parent, the quiet grudge against a brother in Christ, the habit no one else sees. Nothing dramatic. Nothing anyone would call scandalous. Just small things, close by, that we have stopped noticing.

The Song of Songs speaks of the little foxes that ruin the vineyards (Song 2:15). It is rarely the wolf that gets us. It is the small creature we allowed to stay.

God's holiness reaches into the corners of the house. He is not only concerned with our public witness but with what happens where no one is watching. And the good news is that His grace reaches into those corners too.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What "small" thing have you allowed to live in the corners of your life?
2. Are you more concerned about your public reputation than your private walk?
3. What would you ask God to clean out of your home life this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, search the corners of my heart and my home. Show me the small things I have stopped noticing, and give me courage to deal with them honestly before You. Amen.
